B_diminishing_returns.note: marginal gain decays below the step cost; stopping becomes optimal

C_plateau_then_payoff.note: a plateau is not evidence of exhaustion

D_cycle_triggers_switch.note: state change without progress: a cycle with an available alternative

E_late_reward_vs_switch.note: switching on a flat prefix forfeits a late payoff

F_sunk_cost_stop.note: a good prefix does not license continuation

A_C_admissible_bound_makes_pruning_safe.claim: with a verified admissible bound, pruning never loses the optimum

B_beam_loses_the_optimum.claim: a beam narrower than the branching factor discards the unique optimal prefix when that prefix scores worst immediately

D_counterfactual_rejected.claim: a branch whose assumption contradicts the record is rejected before exploration, even though it has the highest nominal value

E_F_novelty_is_not_value.claim: novelty-driven expansion spends the whole budget on mutually dissimilar worthless branches

mcts_decision.reason: the worlds are finite, deterministic and equipped with an admissible bound, so branch and bound is exact and cheaper; UCT's guarantee is asymptotic and would add no capability here

meta_selector.implemented: structural admissibility plus a partial order with explicit INCOMPARABLE
meta_selector.reason: value-of-computation requires a common utility (Russell & Wefald 1991); the four operators produce bits, utility-per-step, invariant preservation and simulated branch value, which are not commensurable without an external preference this milestone declines to invent

A_rarity_is_not_information.claim: an outcome can be rare and carry zero information about the target

B_surprise_is_not_decision_value.claim: an experiment can be maximally surprising about Theta and useless for T

C_unaffordable_information.claim: the highest-information experiment is refused when unaffordable
